items.review_rationale: Read the entire hom-set-bijection definition of a left adjoint, preserving both functor directions and two-variable naturality; did not equate adjunction with ordinary inverse equivalence or an arbitrary family of bijections.

references.phrase: functors L:C to D and R:D to C
bijections between the morphisms L(X) to Y in D and X to R(Y) in C
references.context: Category theory: adjunction's hom-set bijection natural in both object variables

references.phrase: natural in both X and Y
references.context: Category theory: naturality of a family of hom-set bijections in both object arguments

references.disposition: The two functors run in opposite directions between C and D, but neither is assumed contravariant.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the full first-order thickening and universal lifting property, distinguished the source's formally unramified condition from a formally smooth lifting condition, and recorded square-zero kernels and compatible lifts without inventing separate meanings.

references.context: Deformation theory: kernel ideal J of an algebra homomorphism satisfying J²=0
Ring theory: ideal I satisfying I²=0, including ideal multiplication
Deformation theory: lifting R-algebra maps against square-zero quotients under the specified commuting map

references.disposition: Universal quantification over compatible maps to a quotient; the statement itself asserts no existence of lifts for maps S→A.

items.review_rationale: Read the complete fibred-in-groupoids lifting and uniqueness formulation, linked the indexing functor and cartesian arrow concept, and kept the source-specific vertical uniqueness condition rather than equating every fibration with a groupoid-valued presheaf.

references.phrase: lifts to a morphism y→x above f
compatible base morphism between the sources of two arrows into x lifts uniquely
references.context: Category theory: cartesian lifting uniqueness and vertical invertibility over identities in a fibred groupoid

references.disposition: Universal lifting quantification on arrows into objects of C; this is not an existence claim for arbitrary discrete fibres.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the entire universal closedness condition, separated scheme morphism, scheme base change and fibre product, and avoided treating universal closedness under scheme changes as a claim involving all topological base changes.

references.phrase: sends closed subsets to closed subsets
references.context: Topology: closed map of topological spaces underlying a scheme morphism

references.disposition: Base-change universality ranges over all scheme maps, not all continuous topological maps and not only flat base changes.

items.review_rationale: Read the entire filtered-colimit characterization, linked filtered category, filtered colimit and étale R-algebra notions while preserving the algebra-compatibility condition on the final isomorphism.

references.context: Commutative algebra: isomorphism of R-algebras respecting the structural map from R

references.disposition: Existence of a filtered indexing category and suitable comparison isomorphism; no assumption that each map between A_i is an isomorphism.

items.review_rationale: Read the two-way characterization for closed unions of connected components of a prime spectrum, reused the topological connected-component and Zariski-closed-locus meanings, and kept idempotence of ideal generators distinct from arbitrary ring generators.

references.context: Commutative algebra: elements e with e²=e in a commutative ring

references.disposition: The conjunction asserts that T is topologically closed and componentwise saturated; it does not say every union of connected components is automatically closed.

items.review_rationale: Read the whole profinite-group definition, kept the topological group and inverse-limit prerequisites, and retained the stronger topological group isomorphism plus finite discrete structures instead of identifying an arbitrary compact group as profinite.

references.context: Topology: finite groups carrying the discrete topology, with group-homomorphic transition maps
Topology and group theory: isomorphism continuous in both directions and preserving group law

references.phrase: inverse limit of finite discrete topological groups
references.disposition: The system is indexed by cofiltered compatible homomorphisms, not an arbitrary product of finite groups.

items.review_rationale: Read the entire topological-group structure and checked that both multiplication and inversion are continuous for the topology on G, including the product topology on G×G. Neither Hausdorffness nor compactness is silently assumed.

references.disposition: The group inverse operation is part of the group structure; the new condition is continuity, not existence of inverses.
